title: CLARITY GRIDLOCK: Senate SCRAMBLES to pass crypto bill as TIME RUNS OUT
transcript_text: Welcome back to House marking one year since the passing of the landmark crypto industry regulation bill the clarity act It has been stalled in the Senate ever since Senate digital assets subcommittee chairman Cindy alumnus joined me here last week on the timing to bring it to the floor watch Your digital asset market structure clarity act would create a regulatory framework established new SEC disclosure rules for certain tokens Provide greater clarity for the crypto industry and the bill seeks to expand law enforcement tools to combat crypto related Crime by applying anti-money laundering and sanctions rules to crypto exchanges, but you can't get it over the finish line What's the problem? It's taken us virtually every day for the last 10 months to get this bill in the condition it's in today and We're ready. It's very important that we get this bill across the finish line before the august recess begins so we can make the markets aware of the stability That will be provided to them if they remain onshore in the United States to do business This is a pivotal time for the industry and we want to meet their needs So is it fair to say this bill will be back on it will be on the Senate floor the week of July 20th? Well, I expect it'll be that week Jeremy now is North Dakota Senator Kevin Kramer. He is sits on the Senate Banking Committee Senator Great to have you this morning. Thank you so much for weighing in here So here we are. It is the week of July 20th What can you tell us about the status of the clarity act? Sure, so so it's getting a little clearer the clarity act as Each little issue gets dealt with right now I think the the biggest issue is waiting for Democrats to read the new amendments that have been negotiated some of them relevant to To the to the ethics piece of it which you heard Cynthia talk about a little bit. I think in that interview last week It sounds like there's some agreement that the Department of Justice would be the prevailing enforcer which makes all the sense in the world to me and I mean I think the Democrats would rather have states attorneys general things like that I think that creates to disparate a situation to have the clarity that the industry needs Certainly some of the stuff is it relates to the securities intermediaries definition is challenging The industry doesn't like that they they would rather have decentralized be decentralized That being the definition all of these things are nuanced obviously in small details But I think we're almost there Maria. I don't know that we get to it this week But remember the the Senate is in session for a couple of more weeks past this one I know the House has done this week, but We do have a couple of more weeks, but I'm with Cynthia We have to get this done in my view before the August recess Yeah, I mean there are a lot of clarity. They're pardon me. There are a lot of priorities And you're right the House is in their final days of session ahead of the August recess literally they have got Three or four days this week the top priority seems to be passing the framework for reconciliation 3.0 And the president is urging unity in a post on truth socially he writes I'm asking all House Republicans to vote yes this week on the budget resolution Which is an important first step toward getting a budget bill House Republicans must unify and fight for the Save America Act Senator you've got the reconciliation package here that they're talking about that they want to pass again with the Save America Act in it But you also have a real expectation that your colleagues on the left are going to cause a Shutdown and shut down the government once funding runs out at the end of September So you've also got a continuing resolution to deal with to try to fund government and you don't have to deal with a shutdown How do you do that which one is because I know you've got debate on on Wednesday and Thursday in the House So what what's more important the CR or the reconciliation 3.0? Well, I think in terms of importance they're both very important But the CR is a must to do because the Democrats clearly have a strategy to shut down the government again They believe it's in their their political best interest to do that I can't imagine why they would think that But that's their situation so a continuing resolution Which is of course to continue funding beyond this fiscal year deadline which is September 30th into the next fiscal year at current levels The House bill goes until December 4th. I strongly support that if we can get Democrats to support us and get that done That at least takes funding of the government off the table so you don't have a pending shutdown I think reconciliation 3.0 is also critical Our military has been falling further and further behind in terms of spending We have to replenish stockpiles. I think frankly the House bill is quite modest But it's what you know, it's the art of the possible and We should be able to do that If they can get it done I think we should be able to do that before the the August recess as well Although we will have time after the August resource recess to deal with it as well But so the first thing really is this continuing resolution to take a government shutdown off of the table So do you think you'll get moderate Democrats support for continuing resolution because I know that you know You could also see challenges from the Democrats in terms of seeking ice guardrails and other things that they that they want to see happen in order to Support a CR Well, so it's an important point obviously important question And I don't know if Chuck Schumer can keep them all together like he did with the national defense authorization act First time ever that in block every Democrat voted against advancing the defense authorization act Which is part of this bigger picture of course because again You know the reconciliation package funds much of the national defense or much of it is for national defense So Democrats have this this weird strategy I think we can get enough Democrats to support a continuing resolution who are serious about appropriating And that would be much to check Schumer's chagrin. So it's going to take some courageous Democratic senators to do that, but I think if we provide You know a modest timeline December 4th makes all the sense in the world gives us that would give us four weeks after the election After which people you know will now know the the status going forward that provides a lot of A lot of room for for more reasonable negotiations. All right. Well, that's that's clarity on on the continuing resolution Thank you for that, but then you've got you've got the NDA you've got the Congressional stock ban on the agenda you've got Russia sanctions What about all of those and then of course it's reconciliation 3.0 and already you're hearing criticism because the Parliamentarians not going to go for it if you don't have spending cuts there remember the House freedom caucus Wrote a letter to the speaker of the House weeks ago saying any reconciliation 3.0 bill must include strict dollar for dollar And year for year spending cuts to restore fiscal sanity and control the deficit. Is that in the cards So I that that becomes problematic in the Senate because of the parliamentarian as you say It has to do with our rules relating to the bird rule and that that is that policy has to be incidental You know to the to the to the financing piece of it What once you once you get into You know dollar for dollar Cuts and balancing all of that then you get more committees Assigned to it. It gets very wonky, but because of committee, you know instructions That gets copied and then you have voter ramas and you know in all kinds of amendments and then bad things can happen So simple is better. I think frankly I think the House did a really good job on their bill in keeping it as simple as possible I frankly like to go bigger than that But the pieces related to the to the save America act are grants for states to comply A carrot and a stick sort of a strategy. I think that makes some sense. Maybe we can get that done without having to You know to run the risk of not meeting the bird rule But I again, I think speaker Johnson and the and budget chairman Arlington and the House have done a pretty good job of keeping it simple as much as I'd like it to be more It's simple gets the job done You know, it's just I'm just one person, but well understood I mean you can you can say simple like just voter ID, but we know that driver's license are being issued To illegals right now, so I wonder if you have to go the next step and say citizenship Proof but but yeah, let me get your take on Russia sanctions real quick. What's the status? Yeah, so it's as you know, it's always been wildly popular in the Senate I think we could pass it rather easily if we get it on the floor However, I know that with things going they're going on in Iran. There's some desire to put some more meat on those sanctions as well I'd be comfortable doing that But and again anytime you start adding to something that's overwhelmingly supportive you run the risk of losing some people So I don't know what the status is at the moment, but again, this is another one of those things I think we can get done before The August resource recess, but we clearly have to get to work all right senator We'll be watching your work. We so appreciate you walking us through it all. Thanks so much Thank you Kevin Kramer on Capitol Hill
